### 🟡 Changes recommended Attack-ID validation errors can be hidden when evidenceField is disabled, leaving Save disabled with no visible input to clear the error.
1 open issue - [Show attack-ID errors when no evidence field is available](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/pull/3786#discussion_r4521736399) · New
What changed in this PR Addresses #3711 by preserving backend field-validation errors and displaying actionable feedback in PyRIT’s finding dialog, without changing the backend API contract. **Changes:** - Adds defensively parsed `fieldErrors` to normalized API errors. - Shows evidence attack-ID errors inline and blocks saving until the field is edited; displays other field errors in the error bar. - Adds regression tests for error parsing and dialog validation behavior. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | frontend/​src/​services/​errors.ts | Preserves field-level validation details in API errors. | | frontend/​src/​services/​errors.test.ts | Tests valid, malformed, and absent field-error data. | | frontend/​src/​components/​Operations/​FindingDialog.tsx | Displays field feedback and guards resubmission. | | frontend/​src/​components/​Operations/​FindingDialog.test.tsx | Tests inline feedback, invalid state, and Save re-enablement. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: `FindingEvidenceDialog` uses this form without `evidenceField` and supplies `attack_result_id` through `createAndAttach`. If that request returns an attack-ID validation error, this handler hides the message and disables Save, with no visible input to clear the error. Route attack-ID errors inline only when `evidenceField` is enabled; otherwise show them in the error bar.
